title: Negative-First: Self-Supervised Background Modeling for Plant Localization in Green-on-Green Grassland
abstract: Plant localization in grassland imagery is challenging due to the near-identical appearance of broadleaf vegetation and surrounding grass, a setting known as green-on-green. Standard supervised pipelines require manually annotated plant instances or plant-positive windows, which demand expert knowledge,  are often infeasible for small plants and fine-scale features,  and limit scalability for large-scale monitoring. We propose \emph{Negative-First}, a background-first paradigm that inverts conventional annotation logic: instead of labeling plants directly, it learns from grass-only windows and treats non-background regions as candidate plants. We fit a Mahalanobis-distance model to frozen self-supervised embeddings of background windows and mine high-distance windows as pseudo-positive plant samples, then train a lightweight classification head on the resulting labels without manual plant annotation, keeping the encoder frozen throughout. We formulate localization as plant-presence prediction on $64{\times}64$ pixel grid cells, yielding dense plant-likelihood maps from window-level supervision, and evaluate SSL-backbone families, pooling strategies, and classifier heads against a size-matched, fully manually labeled reference. The best Negative-First configuration reaches $0.728$ plant-positive AP, $91\%$ of the fully supervised reference ($0.804$ AP), without any plant annotations. Our results show that frozen self-supervised representations encode sufficient morphological cues for label-efficient plant localization through background deviation alone.
